newsitem.title: EGYPT: Egypt-Swiss sacks firm H1 profits up 41 pct.
newsitem.headline: Egypt-Swiss sacks firm H1 profits up 41 pct.

text.p: Egyptian-Swiss joint venture firm Suez Bags said on Monday it raised pre-tax profits for the first half of calendar 1996 almost 41 percent to 10.37 million pounds from 7.38 million in the same 1995 period.
Egypt's Suez Cement and other main cement companies own 60 percent of the firm while Dipeco Sacks of Switzerland holds the remaining 40 percent.
Suez bags sold goods worth 26.85 million pounds in the first six months of 1996, down from 36.35 million in the same 1995 period.
The firm's nine million pound capital is distributed on 450,000 shares which are mostly held by the cement firms and rarely traded on the bourse.
